h2: NDT training near Ogden: OTECH's inspection programme, Salt Lake college courses and online study compared
html:
NDT training near Ogden: OTECH's inspection programme, Salt Lake college courses and online study compared

Ogden is better served for NDT schooling than most Mountain West cities. A public technical college in the city runs a dedicated non-destructive inspection programme, Salt Lake Community College offers an NDT degree about forty miles south, and Hill Air Force Base with its supplier ring keeps employers looking for trained people. The decision for an Ogden candidate is less about whether training exists and more about which form suits you: full-time schooling, training through an employer, or online theory with the practical done at work.

Who offers NDT training around Ogden?

  • Ogden-Weber Technical College (OTECH). Its Non-Destructive Inspection programme is a 32-credit course on the BDO campus, with day and evening options, rolling start dates through the year and no admission requirements. Coursework covers penetrant, magnetic particle, eddy current, ultrasonic and radiographic inspection, plus NDI theory, maths, safety and a radiation-safety course. OTECH says completers are qualified as trainees under SNT-TC-1A, CP-189 and the main aerospace personnel standard, and describes that as a step toward certification by an employer rather than certification itself.
  • Salt Lake Community College. SLCC's School of Technical and Professional Specialties lists an AAS in Non-Destructive Testing Technology and separate certificates in eddy current, radiography and ultrasonic technology. The opening two semesters pair joining processes with visual, magnetic particle and penetrant work; the later semesters add eddy current, radiography, ultrasonics and computer applications in NDT.
  • A high-school starting point. Utah's career and technical education standards include a half-unit Non-Destructive Testing course for grades 10 to 12 that introduces the methods, certification and an inspector's responsibilities. It is an introduction, not method training, so ask your school whether it is taught there.
  • Employer programmes. Depot maintenance, engine work and the machining and composite suppliers around Weber and Davis Counties train assistants under their own written practices, often after a technical-college start.

Which Ogden route suits you?

Where you are nowRoute that usually fitsCheck before you commit
School leaver or career changer without an NDT jobOTECH's programme, or SLCC if you want a degreeWhether day or evening attendance fits your current work
Employed by an aerospace or defence supplierYour employer's internal programmeWhich documents the Level III files as training and as experience
Technician adding a method or moving to Level IIOnline theory for that method plus a practical at workThat the record states hours by method and level
Supplier certifying its techniciansTraining and Level III examinations at your plantWhether prime-contractor flow-downs change the hours or exams

Five questions to ask before signing up anywhere near Ogden

  • Does the course finish with a hands-on examination on parts with known flaws, or only a written test?
  • Were the hours written to SNT-TC-1A or to a customer's aerospace standard, and will your target employer accept that basis?
  • How much instrument time do you get with eddy current and ultrasonic equipment, which aircraft and engine work uses heavily?
  • Who answers your technical questions while you study: a working Level III or a general instructor?
  • What paperwork do you leave with, and does it name method, level, topics and hours clearly enough to go straight into an employer's file?

Where Atlantis fits for Ogden candidates and employers

Atlantis does not teach in a building anywhere in northern Utah. Method theory is online and self-paced on the Atlantis portal, an ASNT NDT Level III answers questions, and access opens on the day you enrol. You practise set-ups in the Practical NDT simulator, then complete the hands-on practical and its examination at your employer, under a written practice built on SNT-TC-1A, and the employer issues the certification. Common Ogden choices are penetrant testing training and magnetic particle testing training, followed by ultrasonic testing training.

The online route suits someone already working in a shop who needs another method or Level II on paper without leaving shifts. A school leaver who wants lab hours before applying for work will get more from OTECH or SLCC. If your employer certifies to a customer aerospace standard, check with its Level III before you buy any outside course. Suppliers wanting training at their own facility can request a quote; nearby pages cover Salt Lake City and Utah.
